contradictions: PINK1 p.G411S was previously described as non-pathogenic based on prediction tools/overexpression studies, but current data indicate a pathogenic partial dominant-negative effect reducing PINK1 kinase activity.

Previous case-control studies reported more heterozygous PINK1/PARK2 carriers in patients than controls without statistical significance, whereas this study reports a replicated genetic association for p.G411S increasing disease risk.

No homozygous carriers with PINK1 p.G411S reported in Parkinson’s disease studies, yet one homozygous subject exists in ExAC, creating questions about rarity versus alternate phenotypic manifestations.
